findings.label: Long contiguous rows are now vector-bound on the triangular intra-tile reduction (~16 vector ops/element), not on a serial scan
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary, AIV pipes only (cube_utilization=0, aicore_time=0); marginal pipe ratios are not peak utilization and are not a time decomposition.

evidence.value: Block Num=1024, Input Shapes='1024,4096;1024,4095' FLOAT, Task Duration=996.000 us on a steady-state row

findings.inference: Source (main.py:76-80) makes the only per-element vector work of the loop body the triangular broadcast `tl.sum(tl.where(tril_b[None,:,:], s[:,None,:], 0.0), axis=2)`, whose axis-2 reduction costs exactly B=16 select-adds per output element, plus ~1 op/element for `tot` and ~1/B for `coff`. With vector busy 81-91% of wall time and MTE2/MTE3 at 2.7-19.5%, the long-row latency is set by this ~18-vector-op/element budget, not by data movement. Both 2-byte dtypes share the C=64,B=16 path and measure the same 706.5-706.7 us of vector time, so the fp16/bf16 equality is expected. fp32 pays 807 us of vector time with only C=16 (4x more tiles per row), which also explains its 97.2 us of scalar time versus 45.5/41.7 us. Because eval latency matches the profiled kernel to within 2.5-3.5 us for these three cases, this device-side vector work is directly the quantity the official latency measures.

findings.label: The tl.cumsum path costs ~66.1 us of scalar time regardless of dtype (~0.505 ns/element); it is 96% of the short-row kernel
findings.backend_detail: The strided cases also carry MTE2 28.6-35.2%, consistent with the stride-128 element addressing in _cumtrapz_strided_kernel; no byte or L2 counters were collected at metrics level.

evidence.value: 66.1038 (timing-0 fp16 row); 66.1052 (timing-2 fp16 strided); 66.1095 (timing-5 bf16 strided); 66.0615 (timing-8 fp32 strided)
Block Num=128, Input Shapes='128,1024' FLOAT16, Output Shapes='128,1023'

findings.inference: All four cases resolve BLOCK=1024 and scan 1023 values in each of 128 programs, i.e. 130,944 scanned elements, and all four report scalar busy time within 0.05 us of 66.1 us (0.505 ns/element) while vector activity is 0.6-23 us. A cost that is invariant to element width and to contiguous versus stride-128 addressing is consistent with `tl.cumsum` lowering to serial scalar work rather than a vector scan. This directly corroborates the magnitude of the round-3 hypothesis' '~0.4 ns/element' cumsum estimate, and it means the unchanged short-row and strided paths still carry that serialization. It does not by itself show that cumsum is a single instruction sequence - that would require the instruction level, which was not collected.

findings.label: Strided dim=0 path runs its pipelines almost serially: vec+scalar+MTE2+MTE3 sum to ~the whole AIV time
findings.backend_detail: Element-level sparse addressing is inferred from the source's INNER stride and the Input Shapes '1024,128'; msprof block/sub-block rows were not parsed for per-block distribution.
findings.inference: For dim=0 on [1024,128] the kernel runs 128 programs that each touch 1024 elements at a compile-time stride of INNER=128, so the load stream is sparse per program. The four marginal pipe ratios nearly sum to the full AIV occupancy instead of exceeding it, which points to weak overlap between scalar scan work and the strided transfers rather than to a saturated memory system. This is a direction for inspection, not a bandwidth conclusion: no physical byte counts or L2 hit counts were collected, so no HBM saturation or Roofline statement is made.

findings.label: Only the small contiguous case shows a large non-kernel component in official latency (108.2 us eval vs 69.3 us kernel)
findings.backend_detail: Official latency is authoritative KGS walltime; msprof durations are diagnostic and the two collections are independent, so the difference is a scope gap, not a precise host-time decomposition.

evidence.value: 0.108195 ms official vs 69.266 us (and 0.784650 vs 781.188 us for timing-1; 0.998355 vs 995.858 us for timing-7; 0.160493 vs 160.466 us for timing-2)
0.0, 357.079, 115.998 on the first three profiled invocations

findings.inference: For timing-0 the official latency exceeds the profiled kernel by 38.9 us (56% of the kernel), whereas for timing-1/4/7 the gap is 2.5-3.5 us and for timing-2/5/8 it is under 0.2 us. The nonzero and highly variable Task Wait Time between back-to-back profiled invocations shows the device intermittently waiting on submission, so a host/launch component of this order is plausible for the small case. Consequence for planning: lowering timing-0-class kernel time by X us cannot lower official latency by more than (69.3 - X) / 108.2 of the gap allows - i.e. that group is partly bounded below by the non-kernel component and cannot be assumed to reach the 55-61 us reference latency from device-side work alone. This attribution rests on one profiled point per case and should be confirmed by a paired host/device measurement before being treated as a fixed overhead.

performance_interpretation: Round 3 is a real improvement: geo_mean 0.4048 -> 0.5119 (+26.5%), driven entirely by the three 1024x4096 contiguous-row cases (timing-1 -54.2%, timing-4 -54.6%, timing-7 -41.6%) after the serial tl.cumsum was replaced by the two-level triangular-mask scan. The frozen hypothesis is SUPPORTED in direction and roughly in magnitude for 2-byte inputs (0.79/0.78 ms versus the predicted 0.79/1.00 ms), but it under-predicted the fp32 case (0.998 ms achieved) because fp32 cannot use C=64 and falls back to C=16, quadrupling loop iterations. The remaining speedup budget sits in three separate regimes, not in one: (A) long contiguous rows (timing-1 0.324, timing-4 0.408, timing-7 0.316) are vector-bound at ~18 vector ops/element from a B=16 triangular reduction, with eval latency equal to device time; (B) contiguous short rows (timing-0 0.591, timing-3 0.550, timing-6 0.568) still run tl.cumsum, measured at 66.1 us scalar for 130,944 elements (96% of the kernel), and are additionally floored by a ~39 us non-kernel component; (C) dim=0 strided rows (timing-2 0.369, timing-5 1.878, timing-8 0.451) also run tl.cumsum on top of stride-128 addressing, with weakly overlapping pipes. The bf16 dim=0 1.878x is NOT a candidate win: timing-5's device time (160.56 us) is identical to timing-2's (160.47 us) for the same shape, so the gain comes from a reference-side bf16 latency of 0.301 ms versus 0.059 ms for fp16. Nothing here measures physical bytes or L2 counters, so no HBM-saturation or quantitative Roofline claim is made, and marginal pipe ratios are not additive time shares.

next_experiment.action_description: In _cumtrapz_long_row_kernel only, keep the two-level algorithm and change the single intra-tile fast-axis depth B from 16 to 8 (2-byte: C=64,B=8; fp32: C=16,B=8), leaving SCALE, NCH computation, masks, carry chain and the reference rounding order byte-for-byte identical. Leave _cumtrapz_row_kernel and _cumtrapz_strided_kernel untouched so the effect stays attributable to the triangular depth.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Source cost model gives B+1+1/B = 18 vector ops/element at B=16 versus 9.1 at B=8, a 1.9x reduction of the measured 81-91% vector component. Predicted long-row latency: timing-1/4 ~781/776 -> ~450-520 us, timing-7 ~996 -> ~700-780 us (fp32 doubles tile count 16->32, so its 97 us scalar time may grow toward ~195 us and blunt the gain). Predicted speedups timing-1 ~0.32->~0.5, timing-4 ~0.41->~0.6, timing-7 ~0.32->~0.42, i.e. geo_mean ~0.56-0.60 if the vector-time model holds. These are predictions to falsify, not measured gains.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Two distinct risks. (1) The loop body's other per-tile work (tot, coff, carry, two masked loads, one masked store) does not shrink, and for fp32 the tile count doubles, so vector time may fall while scalar/MTE2 rises; if aiv_scalar_time grows faster than aiv_vec_time falls on timing-7, keep B=8 for the 2-byte branch only and restore B=16 for fp32. (2) The carry update reads coff from the last row of the C tile; changing B changes which columns land in each tile, so tail masking and the final partial tile must be re-checked for completeness, and the triangular tree at B=8 must still reproduce the reference's low-precision Add-then-scale rounding. Rollback is a one-constant revert to B=16; no accumulator dtype, output dtype or public path changes, so a revert cannot affect correctness.
success_criteria: Full eval correctness phase 24/24 PASSED (all three dtypes, both dims, transposed and dx=0.25 cases) with unchanged tolerances.
Headline geo_mean strictly greater than the round-3 value 0.5118752032659141.
timing-1, timing-4 and timing-7 each improve at least 20% versus 0.7847/0.7786/0.9984 ms, and no timing or correctness case regresses by more than 2%.

A re-profile of the same three cases shows aiv_vec_time roughly halved with aiv_scalar_time not more than doubled; if aiv_vec_time does not fall, the 'vector ops/element = B' model is falsified and the long-row bound must be re-attributed.
Report explicitly that the frozen round-3 hypothesis was supported (cumsum was the long-row bound and was removed) but that its magnitude was met only for 2-byte inputs.

warnings: Metrics level only: no instruction listing was requested, so the ~18 vector ops/element figure is derived from the source loop body plus the measured 81-91% vector ratio, not from an instruction count or PC mapping.

No physical byte, L2 hit/miss or bandwidth counters were collected; per the evidence rules no HBM-saturation or quantitative Roofline claim is made and the marginal pipe ratios are not added into a time decomposition.

timing-3 and timing-6 (bf16 and fp32 contiguous short rows) were not profiled; their exclusion is justified by the dtype-invariant 66.06-66.13 us scalar time observed across four other tl.cumsum cases, but that extrapolation is an inference, not a measurement.

The ~39 us non-kernel component for timing-0 rests on one profiled point; msprof and eval latencies come from independent collections and their difference is a scope gap, not an exact host-overhead measurement.
The bf16 dim=0 speedup of 1.878x is reference-side and must not be reported as a candidate optimization.
open_questions: Does the 38.9 us eval-versus-kernel gap for the [128,1024] contiguous case reproduce outside the profiler, and how much of it is parameter binding and launch versus Python dispatch?
Would an instruction-level collect on timing-7 confirm 16 select-add vectors per output element and show whether the (C,B,B) broadcast materializes registers proportional to C*B*B?
Is the tl.cumsum scalar cost reducible on this backend by expressing the scan as an explicit log-step sequence, or does every scan formulation in Triton lower to the same serial scalar loop?
